extracted.intended_audience: Applicants preparing grant/cooperative agreement/TIA proposals in response to ONR BAA N00014-23-S-B003
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a research grant/cooperative agreement proposal in response to ONR BAA N00014-23-S-B003, following required forms, attachments, content sections, certifications, and administrative rules described by ONR and Grants.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The project summary/abstract must identify the research problem and objectives, technical approaches, anticipated outcome of the research, if successful, and impact on DoD capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only characters available on a standard QWERTY keyboard. Spell out all Greek letters, other non-English letters, and symbols. Graphics are not allowed and there is a one page or 4,000-character (including spaces) limit whichever is less. Do not include proprietary or confidential information. The project summary/abstract must be marked by the applicant as “Approved for Public Release”. Abstracts of all funded research projects will be posted on the public DTIC website: https://publicaccess.dtic.mil/search/#/grants/simpleSearch

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subject Use (Fields 1 and 1a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal must address human subject involvement by completing Fields 1 and 1a of the R&R Other Project Information form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proposals containing activities that include or may include “research involving human subjects” as defined in DoDI 3216.02, prior to award, the Applicant must submit the required documentation under “Use of Human Subjects in Research” (Section F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animal Use (Fields 2 and 2a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal must address animal use protocols by addressing Fields 2 and 2a of the R&R Other Project Information form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If animals are to be utilized in the research effort proposed, the Applicant must submit the documents described under “Use of Animals” (Section F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Compliance (Fields 4a-4d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address whether the intended research will result in environmental impacts outside the laboratory, and how the applicant will ensure compliance with environmental statutes and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies and recipients must comply with environmental planning and regulatory requirements (e.g., NEPA). With respect to awards that constitute “major Federal actions,” agencies may be required to prepare environmental planning documentation such as an EIS. Most ONR-funded field research is covered by NEPA categorical exclusions. Questions regarding NEPA or other environmental planning or regulatory compliance issues should be referred to the technical point of contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field 7 / Project Abstract handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave Field 7 blank in Grants.gov; complete Form SF424 Project Abstract instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an error message occurs when leaving Block 7 blank, upload the Project Abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative / Technical Proposal required content (Field 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach the entire proposal narrative as a single PDF file (save as 'Technical Proposal') and describe the research including objective and approach, keeping in mind the evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The technical proposal must describe the research in sections as described: Cover Page (must include the words 'Technical Proposal' and: (a) BAA Number N00014-23-S-B003, (b) Title of Proposal, (c) Identity of prime Offeror and complete list of sub awards, (d) Technical contact, (e) Administrative/business contact, (f) Proposed period of performance), Table of Contents, Objective, Technical Approach (describe scientific/technical concepts, complete research plan, what is innovative, comparison to alternate approaches, and expected results/new knowledge), Future Department of Defense Relevance, Project Schedule and Milestones (summary), and Reports (sample: Technical and Financial Progress Reports, Final Report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants exclude delivery of software/prototypes/hardware
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants do not include the delivery of software, prototypes, and other hardware deliverables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deliverables of this type are required, special justification or alternate award mechanisms may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the overall management approach and provide rationale for participation of key team members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe planned relationships with subawardees or collaborators. This is a single PI award; if subawardees or collaborators exist, explain how the proposed team fits the single PI structure. If appropriate, briefly describe anticipated schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a discussion of the qualifications of the proposed Principal Investigator and any other key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevant experience, prior accomplishments, and any qualifications that demonstrate ability to perform the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offeror Responsibility Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must provide information to assist ONR in evaluating the Offeror's responsibility prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe: adequate resources or ability to obtain them; ability to comply with grant conditions considering existing/current commitments; performance history managing Federal awards and extent of previously awarded amounts to be expended; record of integrity and business ethics; qualifications and eligibility to receive an award under applicable laws/regulations; organization, experience, accounting and operational controls and technical skills or ability to obtain them (including property control systems, quality assurance measures, and safety programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management Plan (DMP) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a data management plan (no more than 2 pages) describing which data, software, and materials produced will be shared and preserved or justification for not sharing/preserving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss: types of data/software/materials to be produced; how data will be acquired; time and location of acquisition if pertinent; how data will be processed; file formats and naming conventions; QA/QC measures during collection/analysis/processing; description of dataset origin when using existing data; standards to be used for data and metadata format and content; appropriate timeframe for preservation; consideration of balance between value of preservation and cost/administrative burden with justification for decisions. Include statement if data cannot be made public for national security or CUI reasons (e.g., include statement referencing DoD Directive 5230.09 when applicable). See DoD Instruction 3200.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References (Field 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload Bibliography/References Cited as a single PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach under Field 9 of the R&R Other Project Information form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources (Field 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe facilities available for performing the proposed research and any additional facilities the applicant proposes to acquire at its own expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate government-owned facilities already possessed that will be used. Additional equipment will not be provided unless the research cannot be completed by any other practical means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment (Field 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any equipment available or any additional equipment the application proposes to acquire at its own expense; indicate government-owned equipment that will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify the need for each equipment item. Additional equipment will not be provided unless the research cannot be completed by any other practical means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Grants.gov R&R Budget forms and include option period costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Offeror must use Grants.gov forms (including SF Research and Related (R&R) Budget Form). If options are proposed, provide pricing information for option periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include proposed costs for option periods will result in the options not being included in the award. A separate PDF providing appropriate justification/supporting documentation for each element of cost shall be attached under Section K 'Budget Justification' of the R&R Budget form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Direct Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Itemize direct labor by labor categories or persons with associated labor hours and unburdened direct labor rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide escalation rates for out years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Administrative and Clerical Labor charging
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and clerical salaries are normally indirect costs; direct charging is appropriate only when major project requires extensive administrative/clerical support significantly greater than normal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgets proposing direct charging of these costs must be supported with a budget justification which adequately describes the major project and the administrative and/or clerical work to be performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Fringe Benefits and Indirect Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the rates and calculation of costs for each rate category (F&A, Overhead, G&A, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the non-Federal entity has never received a negotiated indirect cost rate, they may elect to charge a de minimis rate of 10% of modified total direct costs or provide sufficient detail to enable a determination of allowability, allocability and reasonableness of the allocation bases, and how the rates are calculated. See 2 CFR 200.414(f). If composite rates are used, provide calculations used in deriving the composite rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Travel justification
rubrics_metrics.description: For each proposed trip, include purpose, origin/destination (if known), approximate duration, number of travelers, and estimated cost per trip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated costs must be justified based on organization's historical average cost per trip or other reasonable basis and conform to applicable Federal cost principles. Offerors may include travel costs for the PI to attend peer reviews described in Section II of the BAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Subawards/Subcontracts documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a description of work to be performed by subrecipient/subcontractor and a detailed cost proposal for each subaward using the R&R budget form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include subrecipient(s) name at top of budget justification document. A proposal and supporting documentation must be received and reviewed before the Government can complete its cost analysis and enter negotiations. ONR prefers subcontract information included with the Prime's proposal; alternatively, subcontractor's cost proposal can be provided in a sealed envelope or via e-mail directly to the Program Officer at the same time the prime proposal is submitted. The e-mail should identify the proposal title, the prime Offeror and that the attached proposal is a subcontract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Consultants documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide breakdown of consultant hours, hourly rate, other proposed consultant costs, and supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a copy of the signed Consulting Agreement or other documentation supporting the proposed consultant rate/cost, and a copy of the consultant’s proposed statement of work if not already separately identified in the prime contractor’s proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Materials & Supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an itemized list of all proposed materials and supplies including quantities, unit prices, and basis for the estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basis may include quotes, prior purchases, catalog price lists, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Recipient Acquired Equipment/Facilities justification
rubrics_metrics.description: If acquisition of equipment and/or facilities is proposed, provide justification and itemized list of costs and basis for estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable items normally limited to research equipment not already available for the project. General purpose equipment (PCs, laptops, office equipment) should not be requested unless used primarily or exclusively for the project; include a statement indicating how each item will be integrated into the program or used as an integral part of the research effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Other Direct Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an itemized list of all other proposed other direct costs (e.g., Graduate Assistant tuition, laboratory fees, report/publication costs) and the basis for the estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quotes, prior purchases, catalog price lists or other reasonable bases for the estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference/workshop funding restrictions and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting funds for hosting/attending a conference/workshop/symposium, comply with ONR requirements: ONR will not sponsor an ONR or DoD event and funds generally may not be used for food/beverages except exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide list of other sponsors and requested amounts to be funded by all sponsors. For food/beverages, the grant proposal must contain a request fully supported factually per OMB cost principles and the Grants Officer must determine the funding is a reasonable, allocable, allowable expense. Specify how the event and related outcomes will directly and programmatically relate to the Science & Technology Plan and identify specific focus areas to be addressed. Provide technical and scientific objectives and desired outcomes (e.g., proceedings, articles, algorithms, tools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee/Profit unallowable for assistance agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee/profit is unallowable under assistance agreements at either the prime or subaward level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee/profit may be permitted on contracts issued by the prime awardee but not under assistance agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect degree type and degree year, current and pending support, and upload biosketch/CV/resume for all senior/key personnel including PI and Co-PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current and Pending Support must include for each project: title and objectives; percentage per year to be devoted; total amount of support the individual is receiving or will receive; name and address of agencies/parties supporting other projects; period of performance. Upload the biosketch/CV/resume to the Biographical Sketch field. Additional senior/key persons can be added by selecting 'Next Person'. Applications missing required information may be deemed incomplete and returned without further review; DoD reserves right to request further details prior to funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Personal Data / Demographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the personal data form for PI and Co-PIs with name fields completed; demographic information is voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demographic info (gender, race, ethnicity, disability) will be used for statistical purposes only. The demographic information may be accessible to the reviewer but will not be considered in the evaluation. Applicants may select 'Do not wish to provide'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and roles required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants shall submit applications online through Grants.gov; organizations must have active SAM registration and a Grants.gov account; create and add profile corresponding to applicant organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAM registration can take additional time and must be renewed annually. After creating a Grants.gov Account, add a profile using the organization's UEI. EBiz POC will authorize roles including AOR; only those assigned AOR can submit and sign electronically. Track role status using Grants.gov tools. Electronic signature: the name of the organization applicant with the AOR role is inserted into the signature line of the application. The EBiz POC must authorize appropriate personnel who can make legally binding commitments (AOR role), which is crucial for valid/timely submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workspace and attachment format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Grants.gov Workspace to prepare application or download individual PDF forms; all attachments to grant applications submitted through Grants.gov must be in Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not using webforms, download and fill PDF forms via Adobe Reader. Visit Adobe Software Compatibility page for appropriate versions. Workspace allows creation of shared instances, progress tracking, and context-sensitive help. Mandatory fields are marked with an asterisk and different background color. Complete SF-424 fields first so information transfers across forms. To attach Project Narrative in Field 8 click 'Add Attachment' and attach the technical proposal as a single PDF file; save file as 'Technical Proposal' since typing in the box is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: White papers submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers must NOT be submitted through the Grants.gov application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White paper submissions must be submitted through FedConnect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely receipt proof and submission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of timely submission is the official date/time that Grants.gov receives the application (electronic date/time stamp and Grants.gov Tracking Number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should submit at least 48 hours prior to the close date to allow time to correct technical issues. Grants.gov will send acknowledgement and tracking number to the AOR email. Applications received after due date are late and will not be considered. If experiencing difficulties, contact Grants.gov Support Center to get a ticket number to assist ONR in tracking issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient Qualifications (32 CFR 22.415 standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be qualified for award, a potential recipient must meet standards including management capability and adequate resources, satisfactory execution record, satisfactory integrity/business ethics, and eligibility under applicable laws/regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (1) Have the management capability and adequate financial and technical resources to execute the proposed program; (2) Have a satisfactory record of executing such programs (if prior recipient); (3) Have a satisfactory record of integrity and business ethics; (4) Be otherwise qualified and eligible under applicable laws/regulations. Applicants are requested to provide information with proposal submissions to assist Grants Officer's evaluation of recipient qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAPIIS/integrity & performance review
rubrics_metrics.description: For Federal awards where total Federal share will be greater than the simplified acquisition threshold, the agency will review and consider any information about the applicant in FAPIIS (or successor) and allow applicants to comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may review and comment on its FAPIIS entry; the Federal awarding agency will consider any applicant comments and other information in making a judgment about the applicant’s integrity, business ethics, and record of performance when completing risk review per 2 CFR 200.206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide information describing processes/systems in place to comply with subaward and executive compensation reporting requirements in 2 CFR Part 170 and Appendix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities are required to meet reporting requirements unless an exception/exemption applies. Refer to 2 CFR Part 170 including Appendix A for details on requirements, exceptions, and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Assistance Certifications and Representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit Federal Assistance Certifications and Representations (via SF-424 (R&R) block 17) attesting to compliance with laws/regulations and supplemental requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission may include SF-LLL Disclosure of Lobby Activities (if applicable), and disclosure of unpaid delinquent tax liability or felony conviction under any Federal law. The certification includes awareness of criminal/civil/administrative penalties for false statements (U.S. Code Title 18, Section 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding Restrictions on Lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant/cooperative agreement/TIA applicants seeking federal assistance funds exceeding $100,000 must certify compliance with lobbying restrictions and submit SF-LLL if other funds were used for lobbying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification states no Federal appropriated funds have been paid or will be paid to influence officers/employees/members of Congress in connection with the award. If funds other than Federal were paid to influence, complete SF-LLL. The applicant must require this certification language in award documents for all subawards at all tiers. This certification is a material representation; failure to file may subject person to civil penalties of $10,000–$100,000 per failure (31 U.S.C. 1352).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification re prohibition on requiring internal confidentiality agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF-424 (R&R) block 17, applicant certifies it does not require employees/contractors/subrecipients to sign internal confidentiality agreements that prohibit or restrict lawfully reporting waste, fraud, or abuse to designated investigative or law enforcement representatives of Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification language: 'By submission of its proposal or application, the applicant represents that it does not require any of its employees, contractors, or subrecipients seeking to report fraud, waste, or abuse to sign or comply with internal confidentiality agreements or statements prohibiting or otherwise restricting those employees, contractors, subrecipients from lawfully reporting that waste, fraud, or abuse to a designated investigative or law enforcement representative of a Federal department or agency authorized to receive such information.'
